News.title: Four pedestrians & driver rushed to hospital after multi-car crash at shopping centre
News.content:
CRASH SHOCK Four pedestrians & driver rushed to hospital after multi-car crash at shopping centre

FOUR pedestrians and a driver have been rushed to hospital after a multi-car crash at a UK shopping centre.

Emergency services descended on the scene at Mostyn Champneys Retail Park in Llandudno, North Wales on Saturday morning.

North Wales Police were called to shortly before 11am and are now appealing for witnesses following the horror crash.



Paramedics were also on the scene, including two Welsh Air Ambulances, who landed in a nearby coach park.



Four pedestrians and a driver were raced to hospital with their condition currently unknown.

Cops are now urging any witnesses or anyone with dashcam footage to come forward.

A statement from North Wales Police said: “We are appealing for witnesses following a road traffic collision which occurred at Mostyn Champneys, Llandudno today.



“Shortly after 10.50am, we received multiple calls regarding a multi-vehicle collision which involved a number of pedestrians. The driver of one of the vehicle’s involved and a number of pedestrians were transported to hospital for further assessment.

“We are urging anyone who may have witnessed the vehicle being driven prior to the collision or was in the area at the time to contact us. We are also appealing for anyone who may have any dash camera or mobile phone footage of the vehicle being driven prior to the collision to contact us.”

A spokesperson for the Welsh Ambulance Service said: “We sent one Cymru High Acuity Response Unit, one Duty Operations Manager and three emergency ambulances to the scene.

“Advanced critical care support was delivered by the Emergency Medical Retrieval and Transfer Service in two Wales Air Ambulance charity helicopters.



“Five patients were conveyed by road to Ysbyty Glan Clwyd.”

News.title: Two Forest Service workers kidnapped, zip-tied & held at gunpoint for 15hrs inside trailer in wilderness ‘by dad & son’
News.content:
AMBUSH HORROR Two Forest Service workers kidnapped, zip-tied & held at gunpoint for 15hrs inside trailer in wilderness ‘by dad & son’

TWO Forest Service workers endured a terrifying 15-hour ordeal after being ambushed, kidnapped, and held at gunpoint with a father and his son arrested.

The two workers were held hostage inside a trailer in the Californian wilderness on Thursday, sparking a major police response with SWAT, hostage negotiators, snipers and bomb experts deployed to the scene.



While doing field work in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, the pair who have not been publicly identified, were ambushed, zip-tied, and taken to a trailer near Gumboot Lake.

Joseph Henrichsen, 49, and his son Phoenix, 23, have been arrested and face federal kidnapping charges.



While allegedly holding the pair in his trailer, Henrichsen called the police at around 11am to say he had kidnapped two workers and had “live rounds ready to [expletive] anyone who [expletives] with me,” prosecutors said.

He allegedly demanded to speak with the FBI, though investigators are still working to establish a motive.



The phone call sparked a multi-agency response with deputies deploying drones to locate the trailer in the vast wilderness.

Negotiations lasting 15 long hours ensued and ended at 1:50am on Friday when the pair freed the workers.

They then handed themselves over to the police an hour later where they were arrested and charged.

“There’s a lot that transpired between that…At about 1:50am, the survivors, the hostages, the two employees of the Forest Service were released, and I’m so incredibly proud of that,” Siskiyou County Sheriff Jeremiah LaRue said at a press conference.



Police said Henrichsen and his son had an AR-15 rifle, knives, and grenades inside the trailer.

“Crisis situations like this don’t often result in everyone leaving the scene safely,” FBI Sacramento acting Special Agent in Charge Brian Tosh said.

Neither of the workers were injured during the terrifying ordeal but Tosh said they are now “resting and will need some time to process.”

If found guilty, the father and son duo face up to life behind bars and a $250,000 fine.

While the investigation continues, it is believed the pair intentionally targeted the park workers because they are employees of the government.



“I am grateful beyond words that both of our Forest Service employees are home safe,” US Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz said in a statement.

“Our focus now is simple: The well-being of our employees and their families. Their well-being continues to be our highest priority.”

News.title: ‘She was set up’, say family of Monaco bomb suspect as they fear she was ‘forced under fear of death’ to plant explosive
News.content:
THE Monaco bombing suspect’s family have claimed she was likely “forced under the fear of death” to carry out the assassination plot.

Anastasiia Berezovska, 39, was accused of blowing up an oligarch and fleeing to Ukraine before she was found dead just days after the attack.



Vadim Ermolaev, 58, his lover Anna Nasobina, 46, and their son Ariel, 13, were all left severely injured in the explosion which was caught on camera.

Berezovska was quickly accused of working with accomplices, but her family have now spoken out, claiming she would never have knowingly planted a bomb to kill.



Her aunt Kateryna Krasnoperova said: “I think she was set up. Someone must have lured her.

“Maybe they promised her something, maybe they would pay some kind of fee.

“Maybe if they had told her right away that you had such a job, she wouldn’t have taken it, she definitely wouldn’t have gone.”

Berezovska lived as a refugee in Germany caring for her young son.

Krasnoperova said: “She loved her son very much, and she would have understood what the consequences could be.

“Our whole family, we think to ourselves, she couldn’t have done this, or she was set up specifically for the video camera.



“Maybe she was forced under the fear of death? Fear for her loved ones. I don’t know.”



Ermolaev has since broken his silence on the assassination attempt.

The tycoon said there was “no doubt” that “serving officers of the main intelligence directorate of the military of defence of Ukraine” had coordinated the bombing.

Nasobina lost both her legs – an injury the oligarch described as “catastrophic and irreversible” – while he said his young son suffered “burns, fractures and severe trauma”.

A spokesman for the GUR accused Ermolaev of “political statements and speculation”.

Berezovska reportedly fled after planting the bomb at the elite Sun Palace residential building – and made her way back to Ukraine.



Several days later she was found shot dead in a forest close to Kyiv.

A GUR operative Vladislav Reut, 33, has been detained over her killing along with Vitaly Zhikovich, 49, an ex-SBU security service operative.

Reut initially admitted to killing Berezovska – but later retracted his alleged confession before pointing the finger at Zhikovich, who has also denied the accusation.



In another bombshell twist, Zhikovich’s lawyer said the pair have been “framed” and were acting on orders from the state.

Anatoliy Ivanov claimed the pair had loyally defended Ukraine during their careers in state service.

He said: “What desire will there be to defend this country if, for carrying out orders, for doing what you do while risking your life, you end up behind bars?”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Both Reut and Zhikovich have been charged with “intentional murder committed by a group of persons by prior conspiracy”.

The pair were remanded in custody and denied bail.

News.title: Secret prison call ‘hidden by cops’ reveal Laci Peterson’s ‘real killer’, claims convicted husband Scott’s ex-lawyer
News.content:
CONVICTED killer Scott Peterson should be granted a new trial as a secret prison phone call allegedly withheld from the defense could point to his wife Laci’s “real murderer”, his ex-lawyer has claimed.

Laci Peterson, 27, was eight months pregnant when she disappeared from the couple’s Modesto, California, home on Christmas Eve in 2002.



Scott told police he had spent the morning fishing alone at the Berkeley Marina.

Four months later, the bodies of Laci and their unborn son, Conner, washed ashore separately along the San Francisco Bay shoreline near the area where Scott said he had been fishing.



Scott, 51, was arrested and later convicted of first-degree murder for Laci’s death and second-degree murder for Conner’s death.

He was located near the US-Mexico border with cash, multiple phones and a changed appearance after dyeing his hair and growing a goatee.

Prosecutors argued it looked like he was preparing to flee, while Scott claimed he was simply trying to avoid intense media attention.

He was accused of killing his wife before dumping her body in the bay, with the case relying largely on circumstantial evidence and his affair with massage therapist Amber Frey.



Scott was sentenced to death in 2005, but the California Supreme Court overturned the sentence in 2020 because of jury selection errors.

His murder convictions remain in place, and he is now serving life in prison without parole while continuing to maintain his innocence.

Celebrated defense attorney Mark Geragos, who represented Scott during his 2004 trial, said a prison lieutenant overheard a recorded call between an inmate and someone allegedly connected to a burglary across the street from the Peterson home.

During the conversation, the pair allegedly mentioned confronting Laci before abruptly ending the call after realizing it was being recorded.

According to Geragos, the alleged prison call was documented by the lieutenant in real time but was never disclosed to the defense until after Peterson had been convicted.



“I was handed a report that Modesto had been sitting on,” Geragos told The U.S. Sun.

“A lieutenant at one of the Southern California prisons had overheard a recorded call between an inmate and somebody involved in the burglary.

“And they mentioned Laci Peterson and confronting Laci Peterson and quickly cut off the conversation because they realized it was recorded.



“The lieutenant made a real-time notation of that. Modesto never turned that over to us until he was convicted.”

Modesto police claim investigators looked into the burglary at the time and found no evidence connecting those involved to her murder.

Prosecutors have disputed the characterization the call was hidden, arguing the tip was documented and that the defense had access to information about it during the case.

Former detective Al Brocchini has also criticized the theory, calling it unsupported.

But Geragos argues the call and the burglary evidence raise questions that deserve further examination.



“My co-counsel, Pat Harris, always had the working theory that Laci’s disappearance was tied to the burglary across the street,” he said.

The high-profile attorney also claimed investigators failed to disclose evidence recovered from a burned-out van discovered shortly after Laci disappeared.

“There was a van recovered… that had been set on fire a day or two after Laci disappeared,” Geragos said.

“In that van was a mattress and all kinds of DNA and other evidence that could be tested.

“DOJ tested it. None of that was turned over to the defense.”



Geragos alleged prosecutors had possession of the material for years.

“The prosecution has had it for decades,” he said.

“They never admitted it or turned it over until fairly recently.

“Very disturbing on a number of levels.”

Peterson’s latest bid for a new trial was rejected earlier this year, although Geragos said the case is now before the California Court of Appeal.



Geragos appears in the A&E’s two-part documentary, Scott Peterson: The New Evidence.

The film, streaming now, revisits one of America’s most controversial murder cases and explores what the defense says is newly uncovered evidence that could cast doubt on Scott’s conviction.

His current legal team, working with the Los Angeles Innocence Project, asked a judge to allow DNA testing on the mattress and other evidence.

In 2024, a judge denied testing on the van mattress, saying previous testing did not establish that the stains were blood and that the defense had not shown new technology would likely change that result.

Geragos told The U.S. Sun, “I’ll pay for the DNA testing. I’m not involved in the defense. I’m somebody who wants finality.”



The judge did allow DNA testing on one other piece of evidence: duct tape found on Laci’s clothing, but not the van mattress.

The test has so far not produced any publicly released result that changes the case.

Beyond the jail call and DNA testing, the documentary also revisits questions around the timeline of Laci’s disappearance.

They include witness sightings of a pregnant woman walking a dog near the Peterson home, as well as new analysis of the water and forensic evidence surrounding where and when Laci’s body was discovered.

More than 20 years after the trial, Geragos insists nothing has changed his view that Peterson is innocent.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I always believed in his innocence, and I still do,” he said.

“I haven’t seen anything before, during or after that dissuades me from the idea that Scott did not do this.”

News.title: Broken bones, emaciated pooches on ‘death row’ & ‘three dying’ weekly – the harrowing lives of racing greyhounds
News.content:
The number of dogs being euthanised trackside has soared

WHIMPERING trackside, a greyhound is given a lethal injection after colliding with a fence at 35mph.

The pooch, which has been bred specifically for racing, has yet to reach four years old and has spent its life kenneled before being let loose to run while punters bet.



A horrifying study by academic Mia Cobb said that deaths at the track have risen by 31 per cent in 2025 compared to the previous year.

Last year 161 were euthanised trackside due to injuries. It is the highest number of deaths in the last five years, even with the number of tracks operating going down.





The rise in trackside deaths comes as greyhound racing in the UK reaches its hundredth year on July 27th.

And campaigners claim that many dogs who survive the track are left malnourished, horrifically injured and even shipped abroad.

Greyhound Racing Great Britain (GBGB) have disputed the claims made by animal rescue groups and campaigners, saying they prioritise welfare and safety of their dogs.

They also disagree with the findings of Mia’s report, citing that 98.9 per cent of runs took place without incidents.



In 2022 GBGB launched a welfare initiative to improve conditions for dogs following a series of horrifying stories becoming public.

But animal welfare charities’ claim it barely scratches the surface of the issues and the RSPCA, Blue Cross, and others are calling for England to axe the sport following in the footsteps of Wales and Scotland.

Mimi Bekhechi, Senior Vice President of PETA UK, told The Sun: “In Scotland and elsewhere, this pathetic ‘sport’ – in which dogs never hear a kind word, feel a touch of love, and are kept muzzled in barren cages, then discarded like used betting slips – is banned.

“Illness and injuries, including broken legs, heatstroke and heart attacks, are common on and off the track, and dogs pay with their lives for human greed.”

The case of Betty, who raced under the name Refresher, was used by Greyhound Rescue Wales as an example of why greyhound racing should be banned in Wales.



She was found seriously underweight, with serious untreated injuries as a stray in West Wales in 2025, and included in an evidence packet handed to the Welsh Government.

Betty was found to be attached to a GBGB accredited racing trainer.

Despite widespread campaigning to axe greyhound racing the English government is refusing to do so.

In February last year Lisa Nandy, Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport, told Parliament: “We have absolutely no plans whatsoever to ban greyhound racing. We appreciate the joy that it brings to many, many people in our country and the economic contribution that it makes.”

At the peak of the sport, there were 250 tracks licensed by GBGB, but as of this year there are just 16 active ones registered with the board.



GBGB says greyhound racing contributes £166million to the UK economy.

Campaigners say canines that survive the track are tricky to rehome after spending their lives in cages, and aren’t used to human contact.

Earlier this year former racing greyhound Pippa, five, was found abandoned in west Wales, hobbling about on a broken leg that had fused back together without treatment.

She was also emaciated when she was transferred to Greyhound Rescue Birmingham (GRB). It isn’t clear who caused her injuries.

Her racing tattoo had been burnt out of her ear using chemicals in a bid to hide her identity but her chip revealed her racing name, which The Sun has chosen to not reveal.



The rescue couldn’t find her UK racing records, but new from the microchip and tattoo that she had been owned by a GBGB approved trainer in the UK. It was who she was still registered to.

Rescuer Kerri Hill said: “She was emaciated, had sores all over her body and a broken leg that had been left and fused together.

“She was extremely hand-shy and would go down on her tummy and wet herself if you touched her. She especially didn’t want her face or head to be touched.”

She has since had her broken leg amputated and was rehomed to live out the remainder of her days in peace.

For Kerri, Pippa’s situation is sadly not unusual. “We see dogs from racing backgrounds being found in all sorts of states,” she said.



“Many have injuries and are terrified of human contact. When we rehome them, we have to get them used to being in a house, not a kennel.

“It’s just heartbreaking what they have been through to race for such a short amount of time at huge risk to their health.”



She has also cared for Al and Jenny who were both rescued from a ‘death row’ pound where the were set to be euthanised if not claimed.

Both pooches were from the same trainer, and still registered to them at the time they came into Greyhound Rescue Birmingham’s care.

Both had serious skin conditions, and developed kennel cough in the pound. Kerri says she reported both cases to GBGB. It is not known who surrendered the dogs to the pound.

Over 20 years ago, the nation was horrified by the case of Rusty, a greyhound who survived a botched euthanasia attempt.



He was found barely alive, with his ears hacked off to remove his racing tag, following the owner paying £10 to have him killed with a bolt gun – which failed.

A vet determined the only humane thing to do was to put him to sleep. Andrew Gough, the man who fired the bolt gun, was sentenced to six months in prison after being convicted of ill-treating a dog. He was also banned for life from keeping animals.

Rusty’s owner was not charged with anything as at the time it was not an offence to have your own dog shot.

And in 2023, former greyhound trainer Rebecca Perkins was jailed for 36 weeks after she was found to keep 37 canines in disgraceful conditions.

The abuse of her dogs came to light following a GBGB welfare inspection by a steward who said the animals were in a “disgraceful condition” and being “so thin and emaciated” the dog “could hardly walk”.



Multiple extremely underweight greyhounds were found in stable blocks, along with the skeleton of a smaller dog. The inspection found a further four dead dogs on her property.

Perkins, who pleaded guilty to animal cruelty, was jailed for 36 weeks and banned from keeping ainmals for life.

Campaigners say that the continuing of new cases of greyhound abuse shows that the welfare of the dogs is not taken seriously.

GBGB disputes the claim made by campaigners, and say welfare is at the heart of everything they do.

They told The Sun that greyhounds ‘awaiting a homing space’ in trainers’ kennels are checked upon every 4-6 months, those privately homed or retained as pets are checked on at two, six and 12 months following retirement.



GBGB also added any Greyhound that hasn’t raced in 10 weeks while still active is checked up on by stewards.

The Sun was also told that GBGB has a “zero tolerance” for mistreatment of greyhounds and will impose sanctions on those found doing it – including a lifetime ban.

Nicola Jones, Head of Rescue and Rehoming, Greyhound Rescue Wales said: “No greyhound should have to face the uncertainty of abandonment.

“No greyhound should have to endure more physical pain or emotional trauma. Each and every greyhound should be treated with kindness, compassion and respect.”

The vast majority of greyhounds that race in England are bred in Ireland – where GBGB has no oversight of the welfare conditions. The regulatory body says it promotes British breeding so there can be greater oversight of the dogs produced for the sport.



The dogs’ lives are only tracked when they start racing in the UK – once their time on the track is over they are recorded into one of five categories: Retained by Owner, Trainer, Greyhound Trust, Charity, Rehomed by Owner, Trainer, Breeding, and other.

GBGB say that traceability of retired greyhounds is at least as good as traceability of pet dogs.

Since 2021, 612 greyhounds have been killed trackside, according to GBGB figures. In the same time period 380 pooches were put to sleep following vet advice away from the racecourse.

In the same period, GBG recorded that 20,507 dogs have been injured across more than 1.7million races.



Dr Mia, from the University of Melbourne, analysed GBGB’s data and found the increase in deaths, told The Sun: “That on-track fatality data is not covering those dogs that are injured, and then transported off-site, and then may also be euthanized.

“So it would be the tip of the iceberg, but it’s equating to more than three dogs per week, on average, in the last year, were dying on the tracks in the UK.



“GBGB’s greyhound welfare strategy came out in 2022, there’s certainly no evidence reflected in their data that their strategy is having a meaningful impact on reducing the number of dogs dying, even though there are fewer races and fewer tracks operating.

“It’s actually gotten worse progressively over over the four years, from 2022 to the end of 2025.”

GBGB have disputed Dr Mia’s findings. A spokesperson said: “The recent paper of Cobb and Coghlan contains a large number of unsubstantiated and inaccurate claims about which GBGB will be engaging with relevant stakeholders. GBGB data is independently audited; its detail meets and exceeds the requirements set by Defra.”

It’s thought that as many as 16,000 greyhounds are born in Ireland every year – and this is where 83 per cent of GBGB racing dogs are sourced from.

And a report has found that thousands of dogs are culled every single year as they aren’t good enough to race.



Campaigner Rita James, from Campaign Against Greyhound Exploitation and Death (CAGED), said: “We know from the Irish Racing industry that at least 6,000 dogs a year aren’t good enough for racing. They’ve admitted that they cull 3,000 of those.

“It’s impossible to manage the welfare of dogs when they’re over-breeding and culling them at this stage.

“It’s just inherently cruel.

“On top of this, the dogs are selectively bred to race, so the ones that don’t make the grade, what happens to them?

“Racing in England can barely cope with rehoming the dogs that do actually race, let alone the ones that are dropped because they’re not healthy enough to race, or not fast enough, lack prey drive or any of the other reasons they can’t be winners.



“Some of them have to be culled, and that’s just cruel.”

Mia’s analysis of GBGB’s data suggests that the most common career length is less than ten races, with most dogs staying on the tracks for under a year, and between 5,000 and 6,000 dogs leaving racing every year.

GBGB confirmed that last year 5,186 dogs retired from the track, with 3,532 moving into homing centres straight away.



For those that find their way into rescues, there can often be long waiting lists and the cost of preparing a former racing dog for rehoming can be in excess of £1,900 according to the RSPCA.

“What we also see, if you look at GBGB’s data, is that the reliance on the rehoming sector is really high,” Dr Samantha Gaines, RSPCA’s head of companion animal science and policy, said.

“If we look at last year, for example, 68 per cent of dogs who retired in 2025 were then transferred to rehoming charities.

“The rehoming sector is, in effect, mopping up the dogs that leave the industry. If we then look at the cost that is incurred.

“Typically, what we will see is for real rehoming costs for an average ex-racing greyhound ranging from anything from £2,200 and £2,800.”



GBGB confirmed they offer a nominal fee of £420 for rescues who take the dogs, but only if the organisation is approved by them.

This list does not include Blue Cross, RSPCA, DogsTrust or any other rescue organisation that has openly supported a ban on greyhound racing.

GBGB said that thye’ve paid out £7milllion to 100 different centres since 2020 when they launched the Greyhound Retirement Scheme. They also claim that greyhounds start being prepared for a transition to a domestic environment in their early years and support is provided for the transition.

A Dogs Trust Spokesperson said: “Beyond injuries and deaths on the track, there are longstanding concerns about the welfare of greyhounds throughout their lives, including standards of kennelling, transportation, diet and enrichment.

“Our rehoming centre colleagues around the UK and Ireland have seen firsthand the harm this causes, taking in former racing dogs and working really hard to rehabilitate them.”



Mark Bird, Chief Executive of the Greyhound Board of Great Britain, said: “Welfare is paramount within licensed racing and the health and wellbeing of racing greyhounds is prioritised at all times.

“With over 200 Rules of Racing, registered greyhounds receive more protection than domestic pets and we are pleased to be able to show that we meet each of the British Veterinary Association’s recommendations for the use of animals in performance sport.

“There will always be those who seek to undermine our high welfare standards and publicise misleading, inaccurate and unsubstantiated claims about our sport.

“But these campaigners hold extreme animal rights views and are against all uses of animals in sport and wider society.

“As well as a ban on greyhound and horse racing, they want to see the end of service animals and, in some cases, even people owning pets.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As we mark the sport’s centenary this month, we are proud that licensed racing continues to be one of the country’s most beloved sports.

“British greyhound racing is in the top ten spectator sports with people of all ages and all walks of life regularly visiting one of our tracks across the country.”

News.title: At least 8 dead & 15 injured after huge blast at illegal firecracker factory sparked blaze as staff trapped under debris
News.content:
EIGHT people have been killed after a devastating blast at an illegal firecracker factory in India.

The deadly explosion was so intense that it could be heard several kilometres away, causing widespread panic as staff were left trapped under debris.



Fifteen people were reportedly injured in the ensuing blaze as the facility in Ahmedabad was consumed by flames.

Emergency services – made up of five fire engines – rushed to the scene, wrestling to bring the inferno under control.



After freeing several workers trapped under debris, victims were transported to a nearby hospital for emergency treatment.

Officials have warned the death toll could still rise as desperate rescue operations continue.



It remains unclear what caused the fire to start; however, investigators are considering the possibility of various safety violations.

Police have since identified the factory operator as Mehul Dodiya.



It was revealed that under his management the factory’s licence had been revoked, but illicit operations were still ongoing.

In the aftermath of the tragic incident, Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered his condolences to the victims’ families.

“Extremely saddened to hear about the loss of lives due to a mishap at a fireworks factory in Ahmedabad, Gujarat,” he wrote on X.

“My thoughts are with the bereaved families in this hour of grief. Praying for a speedy recovery of the injured.”

The Prime Minister also said financial compensation would be provided.



An investigation is now ongoing to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the shocking incident.

Serious questions remain about how the factory was able to function after its license cancellation, who was responsible and whether safety violations contributed to the deadly blast.

This comes after 20 people were killed after an explosion at another firecracker factory in India.

Around 100 staff were inside the factory at the time of the initial blast with dozens injured with severe burns as they escaped the factory when it went up in flames.

The powerful blast ripped through the facility in Virudhunagar district in Tamil Nadu, India.



Firefighters were able to get the blaze under control, as search and rescue teams entered the ruins to recover the workers from beneath the debris.

Rescue operations were hindered as firecrackers continued to burst long after the initial explosion.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The impact of the blast was so severe that at least three buildings were reduced to rubble and completely destroyed.

Authorities believe the blast originated at the front veranda of the factory, where workers were reportedly handling raw materials to finish the firecrackers.

News.title: Former prosecutor, 75, accused of trying to poison husband AGAIN while on bond from attempted murder charges
News.content:
'BRAZEN ACT' Former prosecutor, 75, accused of trying to poison husband AGAIN while on bond from attempted murder charges

A FORMER prosecutor has been re-arrested after being accused of trying to poison her husband with fentanyl a fourth time while out on bond.

Sara Baker, 75, from Mountain Brook, Alabama, was initially arrested in November after allegedly lacing her husband James’ food and drink with the drug at least three times in September 2025.



Her 11 charges included attempted murder, domestic violence, and elder abuse, to which she pleaded not guilty.

Baker was released from custody after paying her $400,000 bond and it was during this time that it is alleged that she broke the conditions of her bail and tried to drug her husband again.



The former assistant district attorney has been married to her husband James for 29 years, during which time he suffered a debilitating stroke that turned Baker into his sole caregiver.

Prosecutors claimed on Friday that Baker tried to poison his medication when she visited him while on bond, which goes against the conditions of her release.



Per court documents seen by AL.com, it is alleged that on June 11, Baker spoke to one of her husband’s caregivers to get an empty medicine bottle from the house.

The mother and grandmother then allegedly returned the container a week later containing 12 grams of purple powder that tested positive for fentanyl.

The bag she allegedly handed over also contained instructions to put the bottle in a safe place at the residence, prosecutors claim.

After placing the bottle in a safe at the property, the caregiver contacted police.



In court, James shockingly supported his wife, telling the judge that she did not breach her conditions.

“I have no idea why we’re here today, we kept that clean all the way,” he said, adding that via his attorney and the county district attorney, he begged to be allowed to see her.

The judge ruled that despite not physically making contact with her husband, Baker broke her bond conditions by trying to get the container of drugs into her husband’s home.

“Specifically, she committed a new criminal offense by transporting to, and storing at the victim’s residences, a large amount of the drug, fentanyl,” he wrote in the order to revoke her release.



“The continued release of the defendant poses a risk to public safety and no set of conditions will reasonably assure compliance with the court’s orders regarding the defendant’s bond.”

He added that the similarity of the new alleged crime to those she already faces charges for was “especially alarming.”

Baker remains in custody at Cullman County Jail and is due to undergo psychological testing after pleading not guilty to all charges due to a mental disease or defect.

News.title: Several injured as Iran launches fresh strikes on Kuwait as military condemns ‘heinous aggression’ & flights suspended
News.content:
SEVERAL people have been injured after Iran launched a volley of fresh strikes on Kuwait – blasting an oil facility and water plant.

The country’s Ministry of Defence accused Tehran of targeting civilian sites and critical infrastructure as it condemned the regime’s “heinous aggression”.



Iran unleashed a series of attacks against US military sites hosted by several of its Gulf neighbours on Saturday.

The blitz comes as the US marked its seventh night of strikes on Iran overnight on Friday.



Kuwait reported Iranian attacks on an oil facility and a power and water plant.

One of the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation’s “vital” facilities suffered “repeated Iranian attacks,” resulting in significant damage and injuries.

The injured were provided with medical assistance and the site was evacuated, according to the country’s state news agency.

Another strike at a desalination plant sparked a fire forcing several power generation units offline.



It was the second attack against a desalination plant in two days in the tiny desert nation, which depends on the sites for 90 percent of its drinking water.

Several firefighters and a worker were injured while battling two other blazes sparked by Iranian strikes, according to the Kuwait Fire Force.

Flights have been suspended at Kuwait International Airport amid the ongoing bombardment.



“The repeated targeting of these vital facilities reveals a systematic hostile approach targeting civilian sites and vital infrastructure that endangers the lives and safety of civilians,” the foreign ministry said.

The Gulf states have been repeatedly dragged into the conflict by Iran since the war broke out in February.

Saudi Arabia was also fired on for the first time in nearly three months.



US forces blasted more Iranian infrastructure and military targets on Friday, demolishing bridges, a key Iranian port and a spy tower.

The Middle East has endured days of relentless back-and-forth strikes, with the brutal conflict now centred on who controls the Strait of Hormuz.

An interim agreement to end the war has been left in tatters since July 7, when Iran struck ships in the key waterway and the US responded with air strikes.

Iran then announced the closure of the strait, but Washington reimposed its own blockade of Iranian ports.

The collapse of the deal has left the raging war with no clear end in sight after more than four months of devastating violence.



Iran’s bloodthirsty Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) have warned of an even “more crushing” retaliation if US strikes continue.

The regime also threatened to prod its Houthi allies in Yemen to close another key strait – the Bab al-Mandeb at the mouth of the Red Sea.

The move could cut off the main alternative route for Middle East oil bypassing the Gulf.

Iranian officials claimed recent US strikes have killed dozens and injured hundreds, with fresh casualties reported on Friday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The US military also admitted more US service members had been wounded in the escalating battle.



Iran shut down shipping through the strait after the US and Israel launched their war on February 28, sending shockwaves through global markets.

News.title: Police swarm outside retail park McDonald's as five rushed to hospital - recap
News.content:
There were several police cars, ambulances and air ambulances at the scene of a serious incident on the Mostyn Champneys Retail Park in Llandudno

Police and emergency services rushed to a serious incident at a North Wales retail park. Five people were taken to hospital following the "incident" at Mostyn Champneys Retail Park in Llandudno.

Several police cars, ambulances, air ambulances and rapid response vehicles were at the scene. While the emergency services presence was located in the vicinity of the McDonald's restaurant at the retail park, it is understood the fast food eatery wasn't involved in the incident.

News.title: Met Police want to talk to these young men about Hackney murder
News.content:
Met Police want to talk to these young men about Hackney murder

Detectives are looking to speak to Cavalli Harriott, 22, and Jayqwan Stevens-Burke, 23, as part of their enquiries into the fatal stabbing of 23-year-old Elijah Seriki in Hackney, east London

View 3 Images The Met Police are looking to speak to Cavalli Harriott (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

Police investigating a murder in London have released the names and images of two young men with whom they want to talk.

‌



Officers launched a murder investigation after the fatal stabbing of Elijah Seriki, 23, near Mossbourne Community Academy in Hackney, east London on Monday July 13. Detectives are now looking to speak to Cavalli Harriott, 22, and Jayqwan Stevens-Burke, 23, as part of their enquiries.

‌



The Metropolitan Police said Harriott is from Hackney, while Stevens-Burke frequents both Hackney and Grays, Essex. Detective Chief Inspector Dave Whellams, who is leading the investigation, said: "We continue to carry out extensive enquiries to build up a picture of the events of that afternoon.

‌



Murder investigation after man in his 20s stabbed to death near Hackney school READ MORE :

Newport 'murder' horror as woman dies in street and armed police rush to scene READ MORE :

View 3 Images Officers would also like to speak to Jayqwan Stevens-Burke (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

"We are now appealing to the public to help us progress our investigation and would urge anyone who knows the whereabouts of Cavalli Harriott and/or Jayqwan Stevens-Burke to contact police. Anyone with information should call or 101 with reference 4139/13Jul. Alternatively contact independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111."

Officers were called to the scene shortly after 1.40pm on Monday following reports of a stabbing. Mr Seriki, who was in his late 20s, died in nearby Hackney Downs a short time later despite the best efforts of paramedics from the London Ambulance Service.

‌



The investigation is continuing and no arrests have been made at this stage. On Monday, Detective Chief Inspector Wayne Jolley, from the Met's Specialist Crime Command, said: "Our investigation remains in the early stages and officers are working at pace to identify those responsible.

"Police will remain in the area overnight as our enquiries continue and I encourage anyone with any information to contact us."

View 3 Images Elijah Seriki was killed in Hackney this week (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

Article continues below

Detective Chief Superintendent Brittany Clarke who leads policing for the area said: "We understand that this incident occurred close to a school in broad daylight which will be hugely concerning for local residents.

"We don't believe this to involve any pupils at the school and are treating this as an isolated incident. We will continue to update the community when we can."

Mayor of Hackney, Zoë Garbett, described the victim's death as "shocking and saddening", adding: "We know that our residents will be worried and upset, and we are offering our support to those affected by this incident. Our teams are ready to provide assistance to the police in their investigation as needed."

News.title: Debbie McGee is finally ready to find love a decade after Paul Daniels' death
News.content:
A decade after Paul Daniels’ death, his widow Debbie McGee reveals she’s had boyfriends - but no one has matched his magic. She says: “I've had a few boyfriends since Paul died and they've been lovely, but they haven’t been serious. I love men's company and I've got male friends. I go out to dinner and we have a good giggle. I love the attention. But so far love hasn't happened. So, you know, watch this space…”

Meanwhile, Debbie says the legendary magician still plays tricks on her from beyond the grave, by sending her feathers - as a kind of spiritual ‘hello.’ She says: “I feel Paul’s presence everywhere. He's always with me. I see feathers everywhere and I look and say, ‘oh yeah, you're with me.’ I love the idea of the feathers and I would love to think it was true that they're letting you know they're thinking of you. It's a comfort.”

Speaking from their marital home in Wargrave, Berkshire, which is still filled with his belongings, she relays her sadness that his scent has now worn off his clothes. She says: “I wasn’t really aware of his smell fading. One day it just wasn’t there anymore. But while his things may not smell of him now, when I look at his suits or his shoes, that's still him.”

View 7 Images Paul Daniels & Debbie McGee, a magical double act (Image: BBC)

Debbie, 67, worked as Paul’s assistant for 37 years - after meeting at a summer season in Great Yarmouth in 1979 - this included a 15 year run on BBC1, from 1979 to 1994, on The Paul Daniels Magic Show. Marrying in 1988, while they did not have children together, she became stepmother to his three sons, Paul Jr., Martin and Gary.

While she has parted with some of his possessions, she found keeping his things particularly comforting in her early days of grieving. She says: “To be honest, I've still got loads, especially clothes. I sold quite a lot of tricks two or three years ago and I'm going to have another sale later this year.

“I've given odd bits to the family, but there's a wardrobe upstairs that's just crammed with costumes. That's one of the hardest things - to let go of their things feels like you're letting go of the person.”

Paul, her husband for 28 years, was diagnosed with grade 4 glioblastoma, the most common and aggressive type of primary brain cancer in adults, in February 2016 and died a month later, on March 17, aged 77. Now Debbie is a patron of Brain Tumour Research and will be calling on the Andy Burnham-led Government to make brain tumour patients a priority and increase research for funding.

View 7 Images Paul Daniels and Debbie McGee were together for 38 years

She says: “Andy, I know that there is going to be a lot to take on, but please consider brain cancer research. I was horrified to find out that brain tumours are the biggest cancer killer of children and adults under 40, and the treatment hasn't changed in over 20 years.

“This is why the research is so important. There have been such advances in breast cancer, prostate cancer, which is great, but brain cancer is being left behind. When you’re hit with a diagnosis like Paul was, there's almost nothing there and you feel helpless.”

When he first died, Debbie was floored. She says: “I expected to be sad and miss Paul, but I never expected the anxiety when he first died of every single decision being mine to make. The guttering needs doing. Paul used to deal with that. I had to learn quickly. After about four years, I suddenly thought one day, ‘gosh you're stronger than you think’.”

Keen to be financially independent, Debbie asked for work the day after Paul died. She says: “I was very aware that with double acts, once one partner can't work, the other one very rarely keeps a profile or can keep on working. So I rang my agent and said ‘I need work.’ Soon after a kind producer booked me onto a panto.”

View 7 Images Debbie McGee and Giovanni Pernice, on stage at the Strictly Come Dancing Live Tour (Image: Birmingham Mail)

Putting on a brave face came naturally after a lifetime in showbusiness. Debbie explains: “I've always had to get ready and go on stage or in front of a camera when something awful is going on. When my dad was dying, I was still doing shows. It’s like, ‘right, lipstick on, smile, get on with it.’”

Since Paul’s death, her output has been admirable - appearing on Loose Women, Celebrity MasterChef, Celebrity Antiques Road Trip, Countdown and taking various panto roles. Complete strangers have also shown her immense kindness. She says: “Older women would come up to me in the street and not say anything, just give me a hug and walk away.

“Even now, there isn't a day when somebody doesn't stop me and say, ‘We really miss Paul. We watched your shows’. It's incredible. You would have thought people would have forgotten.”

Debbie, who is also working on her autobiography, says, despite their chemistry, she and Paul nearly didn’t ‘happen.’ She says: “He knocked me back for years because he thought I was too young.”

View 7 Images Debbie McGee as The Fairy in Wolverhampton's Sleeping Beauty panto

Now feeling like she is ready to let go a few more of his things, she continues: “That's what grief is like. You turn corners all the time and think, ‘Oh, actually, I could get rid of a few more things.’ My life is becoming mine now. But he will always be a part of it in some way.

“I'm getting on with life and happy again. I have got to a position now where you just accept they're never coming back, and how lucky I was to have had him in my life. Lots of people don't have what I had. You know the old saying, ‘grief heals in time?’ They don't believe that anymore. They believe your grief stays as big as it was the day they die. But you have to create a bigger life around it. And that's what I've done.

“I say yes to everything, I keep myself really busy. With work, looking after my mum because she's 89 now, seeing family, having friends over. That’s what brings me joy.”

And she now ranks officially as a ‘national treasure.’ She says: “On the Queen's Platinum Jubilee parade invitation, it did say, ‘We'd like to invite you as a national treasure.’ That was the first time anyone had ever said it. So maybe it’s official.”

7 View 7 Images Paul Daniels and Debbie McGee, who married in 1988 (Image: SWNS.com) 7 View 7 Images Paul and Debbie pictured on their wedding day (Image: ExpressStar)

When Debbie finished as runner-up with professional partner Giovanni Pernice on Strictly Come Dancing in 2017 - later winning the 2019 Christmas Special with partner Kevin Clifton, she says Paul gave her the confidence to compete. Debbie says: “Before every live show, I used to say, ‘darling, sit on my shoulder. I need some confidence.’”

Her biggest boost came from women’s reaction to her dancing. She says: “Women were coming up to me in the street and saying, ‘we really thought we were over the hill and now you've made us realise we can do anything.’ Eighteen-year-olds said, ‘we want to be like you when we're your age’.”

Inspiringly positive, Debbie still thinks there’s a chance she will find love again. She says: “I'm really happy on my own. But I'm not saying ‘no.’ I could walk into a room tomorrow and suddenly see somebody that I instantly fall in love with. I think that can happen because it certainly did with Paul.

* For more information visit www.braintumourresearch.org

News.title: Iran makes defiant vow that not a 'drop of oil and gas' will leave Strait of Hormuz
News.content:
Iran makes defiant vow that not a 'drop of oil and gas' will leave Strait of Hormuz

Iran's bold statement comes after Donald Trump's forces launched a seventh consecutive night of airstrikes on the country on Friday night

View 4 Images Video footage released by the US Central Command showed what the US military said is the latest wave of "precision strikes" on strategic Iranian military sites (Image: US Central Command (CENTCOM)/AFP via Getty Images)

Iran today vowed not "a single drop of oil and gas" will leave the Strait of Hormuz until the US ends its "criminal" attacks.

‌



The warning came after Donald Trump's forces launched a seventh consecutive night of airstrikes on the country on Friday night following two waves of assaults aimed at easing Tehran's grip on the waterway the previous day.

‌



In a statement on Saturday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said: "Until the aggressions of criminal America end, the export of chemical fertiliser and even a single drop of oil and gas from this region will not be possible." The body also claimed two ships had hit mines and exploded in the strait, but US Central Command denied it.

‌



View 4 Images Bombing intensified in the Middle East for the seventh consecutive night, with Iran threatening a "full-scale offensive" in response to American strikes and hitting several US military sites in Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain (Image: US Central Command (CENTCOM)/AFP via Getty Images)

US forces step up Iran attacks- hitting airports and bridges as death toll climbs READ MORE :

According to US media, the latest strikes hit “military logistics infrastructure”, including surveillance sites, underground weapons storage, and maritime capabilities. Iranian state media claimed the overnight attacks had damaged bridges and hit an electricity and desalination plant in the southern province of Jask, leaving about 10,000 people without water.

Video released by US Central Command, known as CENTCOM, showed several cruise missiles being launched from a Navy warship. The footage also included fighter jets taking off and at least three targets, including what appeared to be a communications tower and a highway road bridge, being hit.

‌



In a chilling threat, a CENTCOM statement said: “More than 50,000 American service members are operating across the Middle East and remain vigilant, lethal, and ready.” The US are also vowing to enforce a naval blockade against Iranian ports.

Iranian state media today reported explosions in parts of central and southern Iran, including Ahvaz, Lar, Yazd and Sirik, while the country's military leaders responded to the attacks by firing missiles and launching drones at several countries in the region. Kuwait’s army claimed they had intercepted Iranian missiles and drones. Jordan’s military said it stopped incoming missiles launched by Iran. And air raid sirens also reportedly sounded in Bahrain.

View 4 Images A damaged bridge lies in a riverbed, following US airstrikes carried out in the southern Hormozgan Province of Iran (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Iran's health ministry today announced that at least 50 people have been killed in US strikes on Iran since June 27. The collapse of an interim ceasefire leaves no end in sight for the war that the US and Israel began more than four months ago.

Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi today said the country has suspended its commitments to the Memorandum of Understanding, which was agreed between Tehran and Washington last month and designed to bring about a ceasefire. He said: "We have also suspended our commitments; we are not implementing them and are busy defending our country."

Donald Trump previously said the agreement was "over" during a NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey. Earlier this week, portraits of Trump, his wife Melania and his children Ivanka, Barron, Donald Jnr, Tiffany and Eric behind US flag-draped coffins were put up in Tehran's Palestine Square.

Article continues below

View 4 Images An Iranian worker adjusts an anti-US billboard featuring pictures of US President Donald Trump and his family on top of US flag-draped coffins in Palestine Square in Tehran earlier this week (Image: ABEDIN TAHERKENAREH/EPA/Shutterstock)

On Tuesday, President Trump vowed to hit Iran "very hard" before threatening to target power plants in the country if the country refuse to agree a deal to stop the war. He said: “We’re going to hit them very hard tonight. We’re going to hit them very hard tomorrow night. "We’re going to hit them very hard the night after, and then next week it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants. Next week comes the bridges. We’re going to knock out all their power plants. We’re going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate.”

News.title: Methanol deaths probe: Laos issues statement on link to 'tainted' drinks
News.content:
Methanol deaths probe: Laos issues statement on link to 'tainted' drinks

Authorities in Laos have issued a statement days after it was announced that a court has brought charges against the owner of a distillery connected to the deaths of six tourists

View 4 Images Brit Simone White was one of the victims (Image: Bethany Clarke / SWNS)

The deaths of six backpackers linked to methanol poisoning cannot be blamed on an individual or cause, officials claim.

‌



Brit Simone White, 28, died along with five others following a night out in Vang Vieng, Laos, in November 2024. Now nearly two years on, Laos Ministry of Public Security claims it was barred from conducting postmortems to establish how the tourists perished and who is responsible.

‌



Two Danish women, Anne-Sofie Orkild Coyman, 20, and Freja Vennervald Sorensen, 21, Australian teenagers Bianca Jones and Holly Morton-Bowles, both 19, and US citizen James Louis Hutson, 57, also died. In a statement released on Saturday, authorities in the country in Southeast Asia said they did no have enough evidence to establish if the deaths "were caused by the actions of any individual or by any particular cause, because no autopsies were conducted on the bodies."

‌



But Laos Ministry of Public Security confirmed that officials had found "excessive levels of methanol" in vodka made by the distillery involved in the case.

Methanol poisoning warning issued to travellers after several drink-related deaths READ MORE :

4 View 4 Images Australian teen Bianca Jones passed away 4 View 4 Images Holly Morton-Bowles also died in the tragedy

‌



It comes after the owner of a distillery in the town faces charges for selling food products harmful to health and operating an illegal business, but not for the deaths.

The Australian government said it was “deeply frustrated and bitterly disappointed” that more serious charges had not been pursued. It is thought the victims drank free shots tainted with methanol, a toxic substance normally found in paint thinner but sometimes mixed illegally with alcohol to cut costs.

The poison is a colourless liquid that tastes similar to alcohol and drinking a small amount can be lethal. Many of the victims were staying at the Nana Backpacker Hostel, where guests failed to check out after falling ill on November 13.

‌



Earlier this year, 10 people connected to the hostel were charged with destroying evidence, receiving suspended sentences and fines of £135 each. Vang Vieng is a riverside town in central Laos and is a hub for backpackers travelling across Southeast Asia.

View 4 Images A general view shows the Nana Backpackers Hostel in Vang Vieng (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Last week the British government launched a campaign warning tourists of the risks of methanol. Simone’s brother Zak White has said: “I don’t think we’re ever going to get to the bottom of what happened and get a fair punishment.”

Article continues below

Australian media reported at the time that the Australian Federal Police had offered to assist Laos with the investigation but were denied. The usual time frame for an autopsy to be performed needs to be two to three days after death. The bodies of the two Australians were repatriated two weeks after their deaths.
